answer.rationale: The two symptoms actually observed are activation -6% and onboarding completion -4%, which points at the funnel itself rather than at price. Two inherited memories bear directly on that funnel (memory_86: shortening onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value; memory_31: cutting signup fields gave a durable SMB activation lift), so onboarding simplification is the action best matched to the diagnosed problem and it is the one I want the archive to substantiate before I commit. I am spending both verification pulls on the memories I intend to ACT on rather than on the one I intend to decline, because an unverified basis for action is riskier than an unverified basis for restraint. What I want from the source records is the effect size, the population, and whether the lift persisted past the first week or was only a first-week artifact -- the consolidated summaries assert durability but a consolidated summary is a compression, not evidence. If either record turns out to be short-horizon or measured on a population unlike today's, I will drop to a small guarded test. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records that discounting bought a 31% activation and 18% revenue gain at the cost of 12 retention points, and it carries an explicit instruction not to generalise it. Against a stated objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that trade is negative, and competitive pressure is exactly the condition under which that warning is most likely to be rationalised away. Downstream risk I am flagging on my own choice: 'simplify onboarding' can silently become 'strip the qualification fields', which would inflate the activation metric while degrading pipeline quality -- the same failure mode as discounting, just routed through a metric that looks healthier. Memory_44 (enterprise converts via sales-assist) means any field I remove must not break the demo-request path. So the experiment must be instrumented on downstream qualified revenue and renewal, not on completion rate alone, and I want a pre-committed stop if qualified-lead rate per signup falls. Uncertainty I am carrying forward: none of these memories were formed under active competitive price pressure, so the prior transfers imperfectly; memory_91 (activation messaging) is a live fallback and memory_57 (referrals) remains the safer revenue lever if the funnel fix underperforms.
